question: True or false: a year ahead, the consensus of economic forecasters has usually seen recessions coming?
answer: False. Prakash Loungani of the IMF checked consensus forecasts for the 1990s: of 60 recessions around the world, only 2 were foreseen a year ahead, and two-thirds were still unseen seven months before they began. Forecasts tend to draw next year as a lightly adjusted copy of this one, until the turn arrives.
move: Treat any forecast of a turning point as a guess with a uniform on.
ask: Which plan of mine quietly assumes that next year will look much like this one?
trap: True, recalling the few who loudly called the last crash.
reference: Loungani, How Accurate Are Private Sector Forecasts? Cross-Country Evidence from Consensus Forecasts of Output Growth, International Journal of Forecasting, 2001
